menu_bug.viewport_tested: 375x812 (window inner: 848x558, matchMedia '(max-width: 1080px)' = true, .menu-toggle visible, .main-nav in mobile mode)
observed_symptoms: After clicking .menu-toggle the nav receives .is-open and pointer-events: auto, but its bounding rect is only ~64px tall and sits behind the translucent header — text appears overlapping/muddy with the header background.
Computed style shows position: fixed, top: 96px, bottom: 0px, left: 0, right: 0 — yet getBoundingClientRect() returns top=31, height=64. The element is NOT being positioned against the viewport.
menu_bug.root_cause: The .site-header has `backdrop-filter: saturate(180%) blur(14px)`. Per the CSS spec, ANY element with a non-`none` backdrop-filter (or filter, transform, perspective, contain: paint, will-change for those, etc.) ESTABLISHES A NEW CONTAINING BLOCK FOR FIXED-POSITIONED DESCENDANTS. Because the <nav class='main-nav'> is a descendant of <header class='site-header'>, its `position: fixed` resolves against the header (which is ~96px tall), not the viewport. So the menu becomes a tiny strip layered on top of the header, with its translucent white background blending with the header's translucent white — making the link text appear to 'merge with the background'. On iOS Safari this also causes paint thrash: every animation frame of `transform: translateY` re-rasterizes the backdrop-filtered header underneath, triggering a full-viewport repaint and the perceived lag.

changes.old: <nav class='main-nav'> is a child of <div class='site-header__inner'> inside <header class='site-header'>
changes.new: Move the <nav class='main-nav'> OUT of <header class='site-header'> in every page template (or every page that uses the header partial). Render it as a sibling of <header>, directly under <body>. This breaks it free of the header's containing block so position: fixed resolves against the viewport.
changes.explanation: The cleanest, smallest fix. No CSS changes needed if DOM is reorganized.

changes.old: background: rgba(255,255,255,.94); backdrop-filter: saturate(180%) blur(14px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: saturate(180%) blur(14px);
changes.explanation: Alternative if DOM cannot be restructured: drop the backdrop-filter on mobile widths only. Removes the containing-block trap AND eliminates the iOS paint-thrash that causes the lag. Desktop keeps the premium glassy header.

changes.new: background: rgba(10,10,10,.96); color: var(--white); z-index: 60; /* above header z:50 */; backdrop-filter: blur(16px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(16px);
changes.newAlt: OR keep white but add z-index: 60 and an explicit solid background plus inset-block-start: var(--header-h);
changes.explanation: Defense in depth: explicit z-index above the header and a non-translucent background guarantees readability even if a future ancestor re-introduces a containing-block trap. Dark-on-white panel also reads more 'cinematic' for a film studio.

changes.old: transition: transform .35s ease, opacity .25s ease; transform: translateY(-100%) -> translateY(0)
changes.new: Animate clip-path or opacity-only on mobile, OR add `will-change: transform` only while opening and remove it on transitionend. Also wrap in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .main-nav { transition: none; } }`.
changes.explanation: Avoids the full-viewport repaint cost of animating a 100vh fixed element layered over a backdrop-filter. opacity-only (or clip-path) is GPU-cheap on iOS.

changes.new: Also store and restore window.scrollY using `position: fixed; top: -Ypx` pattern, trap focus inside .main-nav while open, return focus to .menu-toggle on close, add Escape key handler.
changes.explanation: iOS Safari ignores `body { overflow: hidden }` for momentum scroll; the page can still rubber-band. Plus current implementation has no focus trap or Esc-to-close, both WCAG nits.

lag_diagnosis.primary_cause: Animating `transform: translateY(0)` on a 100vh fixed-position panel that overlays a backdrop-filtered header forces iOS Safari to repaint the entire viewport every frame (~60 frames * full-screen blur recomputation).
secondary_causes: 9 .reveal IntersectionObserver targets remain observed after menu opens; if user scrolls the (now-locked) body before lock fully applies, observers re-fire.
Six elements use backdrop-filter (header, search-overlay, four .hero__eyebrow spans). Stacking translucent layers compounds composition cost.
No `will-change` hint on .main-nav; browser allocates the layer on the first frame of the transition, costing a paint.
lag_diagnosis.note: JS itself is fast; the lag is paint/composite, not script.

other_mobile_issues.issue: .menu-toggle is 40x40px — below the WCAG 2.5.5 / Apple HIG 44x44 touch-target minimum. The .icon-btn siblings are correctly 44x44, so the toggle visually looks smaller than search/contact buttons too.
other_mobile_issues.fix: Set .menu-toggle { width: 44px; height: 44px; } and adjust the inner span sizing if needed.

other_mobile_issues.issue: No safe-area-inset usage anywhere in stylesheet. Bottom CTA bars / fixed elements on iPhones with home indicator will sit under the indicator.
other_mobile_issues.fix: Add `padding-bottom: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom));` to fixed bottom bars and `padding-top: max(0px, env(safe-area-inset-top));` to .site-header. Also viewport-fit=cover in <meta>.

other_mobile_issues.issue: Body scroll-lock uses `document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden'` — this does NOT prevent rubber-band scroll on iOS Safari and causes a scroll-position jump on lock release on iOS < 16.
other_mobile_issues.fix: Use the position-fixed scroll-lock pattern: store scrollY, set body { position:fixed; top:-${scrollY}px; width:100% }, restore on close.

other_mobile_issues.issue: .main-nav background is solid white but no `z-index` higher than .site-header (50). When the containing-block bug is fixed, the menu would still need to be above the sticky header.
No focus trap inside open mobile nav, no Escape-to-close, no return-focus-to-toggle. Keyboard users on tablets can tab past the open menu.
other_mobile_issues.fix: Add focus trap + Escape handler in initMobileNav (mirror initSearch's overlay pattern which already does Escape).

other_mobile_issues.issue: Hero h1 is 61px on a 375-class viewport. Even at 44px @media (max-width:560px), the 'Cinema for the world stage' wordmark may break awkwardly. No `text-wrap: balance`.
other_mobile_issues.fix: Add `text-wrap: balance;` to .hero h1 and tighten the (max-width:560px) clamp.

other_mobile_issues.issue: menu-toggle has no `aria-controls` attribute pointing to .main-nav id; screen readers can't announce the relationship.

.reveal observers continue observing 9 elements when the user is on a tiny viewport with a tall page; cheap but not zero. unobserve on first reveal is already done — fine. But there is no `prefers-reduced-motion` respected on the .is-open transition.
other_mobile_issues.fix: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .main-nav { transition: none; } .reveal { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }

other_mobile_issues.issue: Search overlay input may zoom on iOS focus if computed font-size < 16px; computed at the test viewport was 33.92px so fine here, but verify the production CSS has font-size >= 16px on all <input>/<textarea>/<select> in forms across /contact and /submit.
other_mobile_issues.fix: Add `input, textarea, select { font-size: 16px; }` baseline in the form scope.

other_mobile_issues.issue: Trailer modal (`.trailer-modal.is-open`) has z-index: 200 — fine — but verify it letterboxes the iframe with `aspect-ratio: 16 / 9` and `width: min(100vw - 32px, calc((100vh - 96px) * 16/9))` on portrait phones; could not interactively test the modal in this audit pass.
other_mobile_issues.fix: Manually QA on a real iPhone in portrait; if letterboxing fails, switch the inner iframe wrapper to `aspect-ratio: 16/9; max-width: 100%; max-height: 80vh;`.

polish_recommendations.title: Cinematic dark mobile menu with film-strip motif
polish_recommendations.rationale: A film-production studio's mobile menu should feel like the studio's brand, not a generic white sheet. Switching to ink-on-white inverted (white text on near-black with 4% saffron grain) instantly elevates the perceived production value and solves the readability bug as a side effect.
polish_recommendations.implementation: Mobile @media: `.main-nav { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #0a0a0a 0%, #111 100%); color: #fff; } .main-nav a { color: rgba(255,255,255,.86); } .main-nav a.is-active { color: var(--saffron); }` plus a 3% noise PNG (data-URI) repeated as ::before overlay.

polish_recommendations.title: Stagger-fade nav links on open (50ms cascade)
polish_recommendations.rationale: Each link slides up + fades in with a 50-80ms stagger. Zero performance cost (CSS-only, transform/opacity), feels expensive immediately. Apple, Linear, and Vercel all do this.
polish_recommendations.implementation: `.main-nav.is-open a { animation: navIn .4s var(--ease-out-quart) both; } .main-nav.is-open a:nth-child(1){animation-delay:.05s} ...:nth-child(6){animation-delay:.30s}` with @keyframes navIn { from { opacity:0; transform: translateY(8px); } }

polish_recommendations.title: Saffron underline grow-in on .is-active link
polish_recommendations.rationale: Currently .main-nav a::after underline is 1px ink. Bumping it to a 2px saffron gradient that grows on page-load using transform-origin:left and 250ms ease-out reads as branded, intentional, premium.
polish_recommendations.implementation: Edit existing `.main-nav a::after` selector: `background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--saffron), var(--deep-emerald)); height: 2px;` and add `.main-nav a.is-active::after { transform-origin: left; animation: underlineIn .35s var(--ease-out-quart) .2s both; }`.

polish_recommendations.title: Film-grain texture overlay on dark hero / footer sections
polish_recommendations.rationale: A 3% opacity grain over the hero photo and any dark sections adds tactile, analog film quality. Cheap and unmistakably 'cinematic'. Used by A24, Studio Canal, Plan B sites.
polish_recommendations.implementation: Add a single 256x256 PNG noise tile (~3KB) and `.hero::after, .dark-section::after { content:''; position:absolute; inset:0; background:url('/assets/grain.png'); opacity:.03; pointer-events:none; mix-blend-mode:overlay; }`.

polish_recommendations.title: Shared-element fade between film-grid card and film-detail hero
polish_recommendations.rationale: When user taps a film card, the poster crossfades into the detail-page hero instead of a hard nav. Even a 200ms View Transitions API treatment makes the site feel native-app-grade.
polish_recommendations.implementation: Add `view-transition-name: film-${slug}` to both the grid card image and the detail hero image; one CSS rule `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` and a graceful fallback for non-supporting browsers.

polish_recommendations.title: 1px gradient hover border on cards (saffron→emerald)
polish_recommendations.rationale: Replace the current static card hover with a conic/linear gradient border that softly traces the card edge on hover. Reads as premium with zero JS.
polish_recommendations.implementation: `.film-card { position: relative; } .film-card::before { content:''; position:absolute; inset:0; padding:1px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--saffron), var(--deep-emerald)); border-radius: inherit; mask: linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#000 0 0); mask-composite: exclude; opacity:0; transition: opacity 250ms; } .film-card:hover::before { opacity:1; }`

polish_recommendations.title: Tabular numerals + counter-up animation on hero stats
polish_recommendations.rationale: Stats cards already use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (good!). Add a 1.2s ease-out counter-up using IntersectionObserver — instantly reads as a 'real' agency site.
polish_recommendations.implementation: On .reveal of any `.stat__num[data-target]`, animate from 0 to data-target via requestAnimationFrame using easeOutCubic. ~20 lines in script.js, gated by prefers-reduced-motion.
